note: An index is counted only when its LEADING column is the referencing column and it is not a partial index. A partial index cannot serve the delete-time lookup for all rows, so it is reported separately as has_only_partial_index.
verdict: 67 foreign keys point at clients across 67 tables. 28 of them have no usable index on the child column, so deleting one client makes Postgres read those whole tables. 7 of the unindexed ones are NO ACTION/RESTRICT, which also BLOCK the delete outright if any child row exists.
